result.label: bug
result.what_to_change: In parseStatement, after splitting on \n, only a single trailing empty string (from one final newline) is popped; when the file has a genuinely blank line after the last data row (e.g. two trailing newlines), that extra empty line remains in `lines` and is parsed as a data row whose single empty field doesn't match the header length, triggering the 'errors.rowShape' error. The fix should strip all trailing blank lines (or skip empty lines during the data-row loop) instead of popping only one.
result.evidence: parser.ts: `if (lines.length > 0 && lines[lines.length - 1] === "") lines.pop();` removes only one trailing blank entry produced by a final newline; a statement ending with an extra blank line after the last transaction leaves one blank line in `lines`, which is then parsed via splitFields (returning [""]) and fails assertShape because fields.length (1) !== header.length, throwing errors.rowShape at the row just past the last transaction, matching the reported behavior exactly.

I identified `src/ingest/parser.ts` as the responsible file: it only strips a single trailing blank line produced by one final newline, so a statement with an extra blank line after the last transaction leaves one empty line that gets parsed as a malformed data row, throwing `errors.rowShape` at the row just past the last transaction — exactly matching the reported bug.

input.title: Fix rowShape error from multiple trailing blank lines in parser
input.body:
File: src/ingest/parser.ts

In parseStatement, only one trailing empty string is popped after splitting on \n, so a file with extra blank lines after the last data row still has a blank entry in `lines`, which fails header-length validation and throws errors.rowShape. Change the logic to strip all trailing blank lines (or skip empty lines in the data-row loop) instead of popping just one.
